regions.summary: Tianshan foot and Yanqi basin north of the Tarim: Baicheng, Hejing, Yanqi, Bohu, Hoxud, Luntai, part of Korla, Toksun and part of Turfan.

candidates.name: Yanqi
candidates.meaning: Han-era oasis kingdom (Agni), the Chinese transcription of a Kuchean-language name *Ārke-; also the current Yanqi Hui county.
candidates.fit: Yanqi basin holds Yanqi, Hejing, Bohu and Hoxud, over a third of the region's people; Tang Yanqi garrison was one of the Four Garrisons of Anxi.
candidates.recognisability: Current county name, own zh-wiki article, ancient kingdom and Anxi garrison well documented.
candidates.source_note: 汉代为焉耆国…唐贞观二十二年（648年），设置焉耆都护府，为安西四镇之一

candidates.name: Bosten
candidates.meaning: Bosten Lake, China's largest inland freshwater lake; the name is Uyghur for 'oasis'. Used in its usual English form (pinyin Bositeng).
candidates.fit: Lake lies at the heart of the Yanqi basin in Bohu county, with Yanqi, Hejing and Hoxud around it; the lake itself is drawn inside this region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 379 hits with 新疆, top ones about this lake and its river and county.
candidates.source_note: 中国古称敦薨之浦，湖名来自维吾尔语意为绿洲

candidates.name: Baicheng
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Bay, 'rich'; the Chinese county name is a transliteration. Home of the Kizil Caves.
candidates.fit: Largest single county here by people (19%), held whole, but it is only the western end of a long region.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; no clash with Baicheng 白城 in Jilin (different characters).
candidates.source_note: 拉丁维吾尔文：Bay Nahiyisi

candidates.name: Hejing
candidates.meaning: Named 和靖 in 1947 ('harmony and pacification'), changed to 和静 ('harmony and calm') in 1965; the county holds the Mongol grassland of Bayanbulak.
candidates.fit: 14% of the region's people, whole county, but mostly Han and the name carries the old pacification sense.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 1947年设和靖县，1965年改和静县

regions.notes: Region also holds 21% of Korla (Tashidian township) and 23% of Turfan; Korla goes to region 3.

regions.summary: Aksu city and Wensu county on the Aksu river, north of the Tarim.

candidates.name: Aksu
candidates.meaning: Uyghur 'white water', after the Aksu river. Uyghur form used.
candidates.fit: Aksu city holds 62% of the people, Wensu the rest; the prefecture seat.
candidates.recognisability: Current city and prefecture name.
candidates.source_note: 城市以阿克苏河得名。“阿克苏”直译为“白水”

candidates.name: Gumo
candidates.meaning: Han-era oasis kingdom (Gumo), later a Tang prefecture (Gumo-zhou), centred near today's Aksu and Wensu.
candidates.fit: Territory covered today's Aksu city, Wensu and Baicheng; its capital lay just east of Aksu city.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article but only 28 hits with 新疆; known mostly to historians.
candidates.source_note: 今新疆阿克苏、温宿一带

regions.summary: Korla city (85% of the people) with Yuli on the Kongque river.

candidates.name: Korla
candidates.meaning: Uyghur, 'to look out' (a lookout post on the old road); the pear city. Spelling Korla in its usual English form.
candidates.fit: Prefecture seat; city holds 85% of the region's people and is over 700k.
candidates.recognisability: Current city name.
candidates.source_note: 库尔勒在维吾尔语中是“眺望”之意

regions.notes: Korla is mixed, with a Han majority in the city; Mandarin and English forms agree.

regions.summary: Kucha, Shayar and Toksu on the Weigan river.

candidates.name: Kucha
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Kucha; Kucha was a Buddhist oasis kingdom on the northern Silk Road.
candidates.fit: Kucha is 49% of the people, Shayar 32%, Toksu 20%.
candidates.recognisability: Current city; English form Kucha is established.
candidates.source_note: 古代龟兹王国之地

candidates.name: Qiuci
candidates.meaning: Han and Tang name of the oasis kingdom of Kucha; seat of the Anxi Protectorate.
candidates.fit: Kingdom centred on the Kucha oasis, covering the Aksu and Bayingolin parts of this basin.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 398 hits with 新疆, top ones about this place; but the name is the same place as Kucha.
candidates.source_note: 龟兹国以库车绿洲为中心…相当于今新疆阿克苏地区和巴音郭楞蒙古自治州部分地区

regions.summary: Awat, Wushen, Alar and Kalpin where the three rivers meet to form the Tarim.

candidates.name: Tarim
candidates.meaning: China's longest inland river and the basin it drains; the Aksu, Yarkand and Hotan rivers meet at Alar to form it.
candidates.fit: River begins in this region (Alar) though it then runs mostly east through other regions.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 173 hits with 新疆, top ones about this river.
candidates.source_note: 阿克苏河、叶尔羌河、和田河交汇之处的塔里木河上游 (阿拉尔市)

candidates.name: Awat
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Awat, 'prosperous, flourishing place'.
candidates.fit: Largest county here (30% of the people), held whole.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 阿瓦提县（维吾尔语：ئاۋات ناھىيىسى）

candidates.name: Wushen
candidates.meaning: Chinese form of Uyghur Uchturpan, 'three Turfans'; Tang Wensu prefecture was seated here.
candidates.fit: 25% of the people, the mountain valley part.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 拉丁维吾尔文：Uchturpan Nahiyisi

regions.notes: Alar (25%) is a Bingtuan city with no old roots, so left out.

regions.summary: Kashgar city, the old oasis centre, with parts of Shufu and Shule.

candidates.name: Kashgar
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Qeshqer, English Kashgar, from an Indo-Iranian name (Chinese Jiashiqili); ancient Chinese name Shule. Meaning of the root is uncertain.
candidates.fit: Central region of a 900k urban area; city is 77% of the people.
candidates.recognisability: Current city, well known on the Silk Road.
candidates.source_note: 喀什…古称“疏勒”

regions.notes: Name is the usual English form (Uyghur spoken). The meaning given is not firmly sourced; the article only gives the Indo-Iranian origin.

regions.summary: Jiashi, Shule county (south of Kashgar), Yopurga and part of Yengisar.

candidates.name: Jiashi
candidates.meaning: Chinese county name taken in 1902 from the Tang city Jiashi (迦师); Uyghur name Peyzawat (from Persian Faizabad, 'abode of plenty').
candidates.fit: 45% of the people, whole county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; a Chinese name for an Uyghur place, but the one people look up.
candidates.source_note: 汉名“伽师”则源于光绪二十八年设县时，取唐代“迦师”为县名

candidates.name: Shule
candidates.meaning: Chinese transcription of a Saka name meaning 'new city'; Uyghur Yengisheher. Also the ancient kingdom of Kashgar.
candidates.fit: Shule county holds 26% of this region; its seat is also in the Kashgar area, and the kingdom's name belongs more to Kashgar.
candidates.recognisability: Current county and Han-era kingdom.
candidates.source_note: “疏勒”之名音译自东伊朗语系的塞语，意为“新城子”

regions.notes: Yengisar (Yingjisha, 'new fortress') is 12% here but 16% of region 10, so left out.

regions.summary: Bachu (Maralbexi), Makit and the north bank of the Yarkand river down to Tumushuke.

candidates.name: Maralbexi
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Maralbexi (Maralbeshi), 'deer head'; Chinese county name is Bachu. Uyghur form used.
candidates.fit: Bachu is 34% of the people and 45% of the area.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; English Wikipedia carries both Bachu and Maralbeshi.
candidates.source_note: 拉丁维吾尔文：Maralbéshi Nahiyisi，玛热勒巴什县

candidates.name: Makit
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Makit (Markit), transcribed to Chinese.
candidates.fit: 27% of the people, whole county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county.
candidates.source_note: 麦盖提县是中国新疆维吾尔自治区喀什地区所辖的一个县

regions.notes: The meaning of Maralbexi comes from general knowledge; the article only gives the Uyghur spelling.

regions.summary: Huge desert and southern edge of the Tarim: Yutian (Keriya), Lop, Qira, Niya, Cherchen and Charklik, plus the Taklamakan.

candidates.name: Taklamakan
candidates.meaning: The sand desert filling the Tarim basin; commonly glossed as 'go in and you will not come out'. Usual English form.
candidates.fit: Region is mostly desert and lies along the southern basin; a landscape name does not claim the whole feature.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 140 hits with 新疆.
candidates.source_note: 位于塔里木盆地中部

candidates.name: Keriya
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Keriye; the Keriya river ends in the desert, and Yutian county is also called Keriya County in English. Not the same characters as Yutian 于阗, the old Khotan.
candidates.fit: Yutian is 29% of the people and the river runs through the region.
candidates.recognisability: English Wikipedia has Keriya River and Keriya County; Chinese name is 于田/克里雅.
candidates.source_note: also transliterated from Uyghur as Keriya County

regions.notes: Region 9 is 12% in Bayingolin (Qiemo, Ruoqiang) and the rest in Hotan; Lop Nur lies in Ruoqiang.

regions.summary: Atush and Akto, with Wuqia, Akqi, parts of Shufu and Yengisar, Taxkorgan: the Kizilsu prefecture.

candidates.name: Atush
candidates.meaning: Uyghur 'between two mountains'; seat of the Kizilsu Kirgiz prefecture. Uyghur form used (also written Artux).
candidates.fit: Largest unit (22% of the people), prefecture seat, Uyghur majority.
candidates.recognisability: Current city.
candidates.source_note: “阿图什”为维吾尔语，意为“两山之间”

candidates.name: Kizilsu
candidates.meaning: Kirghiz 'red water' (Kizil Su), after the Kizilsu river; also the prefecture name.
candidates.fit: Prefecture holds 98% of its people here; the river crosses Wuqia and Atush.
candidates.recognisability: Prefecture name; the same name appears on the Kyrgyz side.
candidates.source_url: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/克孜勒苏柯尔克孜自治州
candidates.source_note: 意为“红水”或“红河”

regions.notes: Kirghiz are about a quarter of the prefecture; Kizilsu is a Kirghiz name, Atush Uyghur.

regions.summary: Yarkand oasis: Shache, Poskam and Yecheng on the Yarkand river.

candidates.name: Yarkand
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Yeken, Qing Yerqiang; 'a broad land'. Han kingdom Shache and capital of the Yarkand Khanate. Usual English form.
candidates.fit: Shache is 47% of the people; city holds the old Khanate centre.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; the English form Yarkand is well known.
candidates.source_note: 《西域同文志》释为：“叶尔，谓地；羌，宽广之意。地宽广，故名。”

regions.notes: Yecheng (27%, Uyghur Kargilik) and Poskam (25%, named after the river Zepulshan) are the other large units.

regions.summary: Hotan city with Hotan county, Moyu and Lop edges.

candidates.name: Hotan
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Xoten (Khotan); ancient Kingdom of Khotan, centre of jade and silk. Written Hotan; Khotan is the older spelling.
candidates.fit: City 50% of the people, with Hotan county 24%.
candidates.recognisability: Current city and prefecture name.
candidates.source_note: 古代于阗王国是世界上最早的佛教国家之一

regions.summary: Moyu, Pishan and Yecheng foothills along the Karakash river west of Hotan.

candidates.name: Karakash
candidates.meaning: Uyghur Qaraqash, 'black jade'; Moyu is the Chinese translation. Named after the Karakash river, famous for jade.
candidates.fit: Moyu is 47% of the people; the river passes through the county.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, county and river both known as Moyu.
candidates.source_note: 即「黑玉河」之意，因出产墨玉又名墨玉河

candidates.name: Pishan
candidates.meaning: Han-era oasis kingdom of Pishan (Uyghur Guma); the county keeps the old name.
candidates.fit: Pishan is 33% of the people and 60% of the area, held whole.
candidates.recognisability: Current county with an ancient kingdom of the same name.
candidates.source_note: 汉朝时王治皮山城（今新疆皮山县东南）。属西域都护

regions.notes: Moyu town sits in region 12, so Karakash fits through the river and county more than the town.
